meta._note: SEED FILE. Values carried from the UK design mockups. Most are placeholder/illustrative and MUST be replaced with researched data. Tags below say which.

_meta.source: statutory rates are held (see tax_detail); total_pct and its components are a blended small-company estimate
_meta.method: IDENTITY: total_pct = sum(components) = 19 (corporation) + 5 (rates-equiv) + 8 (dividend) + 4 (capital-gains-equiv) = 36. Components are modeled profit-equivalent ANNUAL WEIGHTS for a typical small company, not statutory rates (statutory rates live in tax_detail); employer on-cost and customer VAT are excluded from total

tax_burden.notes: VAT is customer-borne and excluded from total_pct. Components sum to total_pct by construction, so each one reads as a coherent share of the load. capital_gains_pct is an annualized exit-tax equivalent, NOT the 20% statutory CGT rate; business_rates_pct_equiv is a profit-equivalent estimate, refine with real rateable-value data.

_meta.source: World Bank Doing Business 2020 EoDB score 83.5 (rank 8); WGI government effectiveness 1.18, political stability 0.26; domestic credit to private sector ~130% GDP; VC 2024 ~9.4B USD (3rd globally); GDP/cap PPP 62009, growth 0.8%, labour force 35M; price level above OECD avg
_meta.method: ease_of_business 8: EoDB 83.5, fast company formation and strong common-law contract enforcement. talent_pool 8: 35M labour force, top universities and finance/tech skills depth. access_to_financing 8: deep capital markets, credit ~130% GDP and Europe-leading VC ~9.4B. political_stability 7: effective institutions, post-Brexit policy churn tempers the score. economic_reward 7: high GDP/cap PPP 62009 and large services market, 0.8% growth. affordability 4: above-OECD price level, London costs are high.

_meta.source: registration fee + bank names are held; timings estimated
_meta.method: IDENTITY: total_days = the day the slowest setup step clears. Registration completes day 1, tax registration day 2, and the bank account (started day 1, ~21 days of checks) clears about day 21, so days-to-fully-set-up = 21. VAT waits until sales pass the threshold, so it sits outside total_days

steps.name: Register for VAT (if sales are high)

banking.notes: Slow step for foreign-owned firms; a UK-resident director or address is often required.
bullets: A UK-resident director or address is usually needed to open an account.
Digital banks (Starling, Tide, Monzo) approve in days; high-street banks take 2 to 4 weeks.
Every director gives proof of ID, address and business activity.
Most digital banks ask no minimum deposit.

notes.hire: Flexible hiring with light onboarding paperwork; written statement of particulars due day one and a right-to-work check required.
notes.contract: Permanent, fixed-term and zero-hours contracts all permitted; probation periods are common and freely set.
notes.fire: Two years of service unlocks unfair-dismissal protection, so dismissals after that need a fair reason and process; statutory redundancy pay applies. Notice and process are lighter than in continental peers.
notes.recruiting: Large, mobile labour market with deep white-collar supply, strong English-language pipeline and active recruitment channels.

_meta.source: Pay modeled from OECD average annual wages (UK ~63.7k USD PPP, 2024) and national mean earnings ~44k GBP, plus employer National Insurance 15 percent (2025/26) and auto-enrolment pension; hire/fire from OECD employment protection indicators (UK among least strict, unfair-dismissal qualifying period two years); languages from ONS Census 2021 (English main language 91.1 percent; Welsh speakers in Wales 17.8 percent, ~1 percent UK-wide).
_meta.method: Triangulated wage benchmarks and statutory on-costs converted to USD at fx 1.322872; talent_depth scored 1-5 from STEM-graduate output, sector employment and cluster strength; languages native-only from census main-language data.

_raw._pay_note: Fully-loaded annual employer cost in USD: representative white-collar gross salary by level plus employer on-costs of roughly 18 to 20 percent (employer National Insurance at 15 percent above a low threshold plus auto-enrolment pension). Base gross anchored on national average earnings around 44k GBP with white-collar premiums by level. Converted from GBP at 1.322872.
_raw._talent_signal: finance: global financial centre with one of the world's largest banking and asset-management workforces. software_tech: ~250k STEM graduates a year and Europe's largest tech-investment hub. professional_legal: leading global legal and consulting market. creative_media: world-leading advertising, film and media cluster. life_sciences: top-six pharma employer with strong research base but mid-size manufacturing. manufacturing_trades: smaller industrial base, ~9 percent of GDP and below-peer engineering graduate share.

_meta.source: Median equivalised disposable income 26,884 USD PPP (OECD income distribution database 2021, cross-checked against the published cross-country compilation) = HELD. Gini 0.331 for disposable income post-tax-and-transfer (national household finances survey, financial year ending 2023; 0.329 in FYE2024) = HELD, consistent with the OECD figure of 0.354 (2021, pre-recent decline). Average 32,275 and top10 80,437 and top1 137,358 = MODELED lognormal from median and Gini. Household spend from the national family-spending release April 2023 to March 2024 (total 623.30 per week: housing+fuel 18 pct, transport 14 pct, food+non-alcoholic 11 pct, restaurants/hotels 7 pct).
_meta.method: Median held from official statistics. Mean derived as median times exp(sigma^2/2); top-decile and top-percentile as conditional means above the P90 and P99 lognormal thresholds. Spend shares mapped to seven fixed buckets normalized to 100.

_raw.income_basis: Annual equivalised disposable income per person (individual basis), USD at purchasing power parity. Median is the OECD equivalised disposable income; average and the top-decile and top-percentile figures are the conditional means of the same distribution.

_meta.source: Energy: GlobalPetrolPrices business tariff GBP 0.306/kWh (Sep 2025, all-in incl distribution+taxes) and DESNZ Quarterly Energy Prices non-domestic average ~24-30 p/kWh (2025); representative all-in set at GBP 0.30/kWh. Rent: London City prime office ~GBP 100/sqft/yr (Savills/SHB Real Estate Q3 2025), secondary Grade B GBP 40-65/sqft; representative prime set GBP 1050/sqm/yr (GBP ~97.5/sqft x 10.7639). Labour: ONS ASHE 2025 mean full-time gross ~GBP 43k + employer NI 15% and pension auto-enrolment (loaded x1.15) = GBP 49,450; cross-checked vs Eurostat-style hourly. Setup: IDENTITY: license_setup_usd = company registration GBP 12 ($16, the setup-timeline fee) + a representative trade licence GBP 100 ($132, tax_detail fixed fees) = GBP 112 -> $148 all-in licence & setup.
_meta.method: Local currency to USD with fx_to_usd 1.322872. Rent from GBP/sqft x 10.7639 to GBP/sqm then to USD. Labour = avg gross wage x employer-burden multiplier 1.15, then to USD. Energy is all-in commercial unit rate. London is the representative commercial city.

bullets: Mature broker market; most small firms sell in 6 to 12 months.
Buyers price a small business at x2 to x3.5 a year's profit.
Clean books and a transferable customer base lift the price most.
Asset sales suit micro-firms; share sales suit larger ones.

_meta.source: Energy: industrial electricity about 26-27 p/kWh, the highest among 25 reporting economies and well above the IEA median (IEA; cross-source). Exit: deep, mature broker market with a broad buyer pool; typical small-business sale takes about 6-12 months. Skills: persistent recruitment difficulty and post-Brexit labour gaps. Rule/tax: frequent fiscal changes including rising employer national insurance and higher capital-gains treatment on business-asset disposals. Demand: weak 0.8% real growth with above-target inflation (3.2%). Currency: GBP floating, moderate volatility. Multiples set to a small-business SDE range (about 1.5x-3.5x typical).
_meta.method: Held on energy (IEA highest-of-peers, multi-source) and on the active broker market and 6-12 month sale window; risk scores normalized across the peer set; multiples narrowed to small-business SDE.

character.the_catch: The 19% headline tax is only part of the story: add business rates, dividend tax and the rest and the all-in load runs nearer 36%, a gap every operator already here has priced in.
character._the_catch_note: Dedicated honesty-band sentence for The Catch's third bullet. It must stay DISTINCT from every locals_intel item (those render verbatim in 'What locals know') and must only restate figures already on the page (hero 19% corporation tax, tax_burden.total_pct 36).

locals_intel.title: Price the hidden costs first.
locals_intel.detail: Energy and business rates catch new owners out; local operators budget for them before they sign a lease, not after.

locals_intel.title: The bank account is the bottleneck.
locals_intel.detail: Everything else moves fast, so start the account application on day one; a digital bank clears faster than the high street.

locals_intel.title: Two years changes the rules.
locals_intel.detail: Employees gain unfair-dismissal rights at two years of service, so most firms use probation and fixed terms deliberately early on.

locals_intel.title: London is not the only market.
locals_intel.detail: Rents and wages fall sharply outside the south east while demand holds up.

_meta.source: Positions modeled from CPI 2024 score 71 (rank 20) and WJP Rule of Law Index 2024 rank 15 of 142 (score 0.78) for gov_business; Hofstede dimensions (individualism 89, power distance 35, uncertainty avoidance 35, direct but understated, casual-leaning) for culture_outsider. Spectra fixed for cross-country comparison.
_meta.method: Governance percentile rank mapped to 0-1 (top-tier clean dealing, strong common-law courts, lighter paperwork and easier enforcement; tax mid given complexity); culture positions from cross-cultural dimension scores (direct but polite/understated, casual-leaning, rules-led, brisk, quick to transact).
